deviations_from_plan: R1 tolerance: the plan asks +-1e-9 m. The acceptance is tol(len, X) = 1e-9 m + 8 u S X / max(len, 1e-12 m), capped at len + 1e-9 m, with u = 2^-53, S = 72.9 m and X = max(S, largest |endpoint coordinate| of the segment). The extra term is the unavoidable double-precision error of a millimetre-long, near-tangent chord (rounding an endpoint moves the line by u X): it is 4.7e-9 m at len = 1 mm for X = S, grows in proportion to X, and is at most 2.9e-10 m for len >= 5 cm and X <= 220 m. The first version used X = S for every segment and failed seeds 12 and 13 at N = 1e5 (errors of 5e-9 to 8e-9 m at len = 1 mm and X = 135 to 220 m).

C9 (reversal): the plan asks 1e-12 relative. The test uses 1e-12 * max(len) + 128 u (|a| + |b|): a length built from coordinates of size |a|, |b| cannot be reproduced better than the rounding of those coordinates, and near-tangent chords amplify it. The worst difference against a long-double evaluation is 1.3e-11 m over 1e5 segments up to 5 km long, far inside the 1e-9 m acceptance.
V (volume by parallel-line grids), release build: 1 m^3 as in the plan, with h = 0.01 (vertical lines), 0.02 (lines along x and along detector-centroid) and 0.05 (dense body alone).

V, sanitizer build (--fast): coarser grids (h = 0.02, 0.04, 0.04 and 0.1) and a tolerance of 2 m^3 instead of 1 m^3; that build exercises the code for memory and undefined behaviour, and the 1 m^3 acceptance is the release build's.
